newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican gov't sees new corn subsidy scheme in Aug.
newsitem.headline: Mexican gov't sees new corn subsidy scheme in Aug.

text.p: A top official in Mexico's trade ministry on Thursday said a new corn and corn-flour subsidy system using electronic cards will be introduced in August.

Israel Gutierrez Guerrero, deputy interior trade minister, told reporters the new system would give tortilla makers the right to choose which raw material -- corn or corn-flour -- they use to make the pancake-like staple.

Mexico's largest corn-flour producer Maseca on Wednesday said the new system would be introduced in June, though its CFO Javier Velez on Thursday acknowledged that the government had issued no official document setting the launch date in stone.
Gutierrez Guerrero said the new system did not imply a lifting of tortilla subsidies, that are used to keep prices within reach of Mexico's poorest who eat tortillas more than bread.
"The official price of 1.70 pesos (per kilo) will be respected," the official said.
